solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Architect Mark does houses?

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it within, so the deer surround the mark

parts.note: does are female deer, so the word stands for DEER
a sign is a mark or symbol

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an architect leaves a personal mark on the houses they build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is a person who plans buildings, a kind of designer.

clue.text: Singular slander used to upset? There there!

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the column of letters over, so the pieces read from the bottom up

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
to sling mud is to slander, so mud stands for slander
'did' as in 'used to do' or 'did drugs'; the blog reads 'used to' as DID

explanation.surface: A single smear is employed to wound someone, and a voice offers soothing comfort afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Said to a crying child, or mockingly to a sulking adult, it is a soothing exclamation of sympathy like 'there there'.

clue.text: Source of light embodied by Helios, unsurprisingly

indicators.note: something embodied by these words sits inside their letters, here across the word break

explanation.surface: The Greek sun god Helios naturally personifies the light-giver.
explanation.walkthrough: Helios is the Greek god of the sun, so the surface is true as well as cryptic.
explanation.definitionFit: Our star gives the daylight, the primary natural light source on Earth.

clue.text: Something native to China in wok, perhaps? Starters of dubious authenticity

parts.note: a wok is a large round cooking pan, so jokingly a giant one

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether a Chinese dish cooked in a wok is authentic, given its dubious starters.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Chinese cooking; China's animal is the real subject.
explanation.definitionFit: This black-and-white bear lives wild only in the mountain forests of central China.

clue.text: Praise levy once cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife, so once gives EX

indicators.note: cut means the word for levy loses its final letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge levied for use of a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Praise for a tax that was once reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud or glorify, a verb of praising.

clue.text: Torn to pieces, as may be a roof?

definitions.meaning: criticised harshly, as a review savages a play

explanation.surface: Something ripped apart, perhaps a roof in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being savaged by critics is a common British idiom for harsh criticism; a slate-covered roof is literally so.

clue.text: Cut around circular line forming ring

indicators.note: around means the word for cut goes round the circle letter

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch
O is round in shape, so circular gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A circular line, like a railway route, cut to form a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve of string or track that comes back to cross itself makes a closed circle.

clue.text: Criminal in the end, dirt cheap

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the next word only

parts.note: reasonable means fairly priced, inexpensive

explanation.surface: Someone notes that something was, in the end, dirt cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirt cheap' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonable acts betray one's country, so they are criminal, punishable offences.

clue.text: Misery guts in tiresome couple supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece for couple sits below, holding up what is above it
the guts are the innermost letters of the word tiresome

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A misery guts is moaning, while a tiresome couple props up their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misery guts' is a British phrase for a grumbler; split it, with 'Misery' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopeless wretchedness is a state of misery, the loss of all hope.

clue.text: Happy to be ushered past beastly noise

indicators.note: past puts the guided piece after the noise

parts.note: a grunt is the noise a pig makes
to usher is to lead someone in

explanation.surface: A happy person is shown past a pig's snort.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a jokey back-formation from 'disgruntled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the jocular opposite of disgruntled, it means pleased or satisfied.

clue.text: Side on wheel clamped by those transporting stock

indicators.note: clamped by means held inside the word for those moving stock

parts.note: drovers drive cattle or sheep to market
a caster is a small swivelling wheel on furniture

explanation.surface: A side panel on a wheel is clamped by cattle-truck operators.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a football club from Doncaster in South Yorkshire; 'side' means team.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is a team, and this is an English football team.

clue.text: Disturbing improvisation of lutenist, no good

indicators.note: an improvisation reworks the material freely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lute player's improvising is no good and rather disturbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that unnerves or upsets is disturbing in the sense of troubling.

clue.text: Girl spilled rum onto head of this fish

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

indicators.note: spilled means these letters are scattered and rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl spills rum over the head of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea trout are also called by this name, a species of fish.

clue.text: Continent first of all in Africa, second is Antarctica

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A geography fact: Africa comes first and Antarctica second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second is' looks like ranking talk but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of Earth's great landmasses, stretching from Turkey to Japan.

clue.text: Prior to functions, bag up some empty dishes

indicators.note: prior to places these pieces before the word for functions
in a down clue up means read bottom to top

parts.note: a sac is a bag, as in a pouch in a body

indicators.note: empty means take only the outer letters

parts.note: roles are functions or jobs

explanation.surface: Before an event, someone bags up some empty dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cooking vessels and the slow-cooked stews made in them, both dishes.

clue.text: Royal, sweet little thing

definitions.meaning: a wife, mother or daughter of a sultan

explanation.surface: A darling little princess is called sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's consort is a royal woman; the dried grape is a small sweet fruit.

clue.text: Fundamental part of nature to pocket money without prior arrangement

indicators.note: to pocket means to take in, so the money goes inside

parts.note: an atom is a basic building block of matter
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A basic natural principle is to grab money without a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Done haphazardly or by chance, with no plan or pattern behind it.

clue.text: Librettist inspiring a neophyte

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the librettist takes the letter in

parts.note: Alan Jay Lerner wrote the words for My Fair Lady

explanation.surface: A lyricist inspires a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or novice, someone still being taught.

clue.text: Wine knocked over by a hundred despicable cats, all together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
low means mean or contemptible

indicators.note: knocked over means the word for wine is upturned and read backwards

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: Wine is upset by a hundred nasty cats together.
explanation.definitionFit: A collective noun: a group of felines is called by this rare word.

clue.text: Flower from the edge of Hereford?

indicators.note: of means the edge belongs to the animal, so the animal piece comes first

parts.note: a Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, so Hereford's gives COW'S
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A flower picked from the border of a Herefordshire field.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford looks like the English city or county; it is the cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow wild spring plant of English meadows, a primula.

clue.text: South of France recalled disease in rubbish collector

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the French word is reversed

parts.note: sud is French for south
TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: A disease in the south of France was recalled in a rubbish collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A bin for household waste collects the rubbish, a British term for a garbage can.

clue.text: Indeed canning goes wrong for spray

indicators.note: canning means holding inside a container

parts.note: nay can mean 'indeed, even more', as in 'many, nay most'

indicators.note: wrong signals that these letters go awry

explanation.surface: Indeed, a canning operation goes wrong with a spray.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray of flowers is a small bunch or posy.

clue.text: Power unit, where I didn't hear sounds

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is heard like the word used

parts.note: what? is what one says on failing to hear

explanation.surface: Someone missed hearing which unit of power was meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of power, one joule per second.

clue.text: Discrimination, quality of a brunette might you say?

definitions.text: quality of a brunette might you say?
definitions.meaning: a brunette is not blonde, so jokingly not fair-haired

explanation.surface: A question about the quality of a dark-haired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is injustice; and a dark-haired person lacks the fair-haired quality.

clue.text: A desire that I will immediately succeed

parts.note: an itch is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Someone longs to succeed straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means follow: in the alphabet I comes straight after this letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter H is spelt out this way, and I follows it in the alphabet.

clue.text: Slug in bottom of glass with syrup

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: syrup of figs is Cockney rhyming slang for a wig

explanation.surface: A slug lies at the bottom of a glass of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup, short for 'syrup of figs', is British rhyming slang for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug of drink is a large gulp, a swallow.

clue.text: Doubly OK with gallons in a stew that's rich!

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble, so these letters are mixed
doubly means the two letters are given twice

explanation.surface: A double OK for a rich stew with gallons of stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Both exclamations mock hypocrisy, accusing a critic of the same fault.

clue.text: Gloriana stands for wrath

indicators.note: in a down clue standing upright means read upward

parts.note: Gloriana was a name for Elizabeth I, Elizabeth Regina the First, ER I

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth I represents fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloriana is Spenser's name for Elizabeth I in The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is anger or fury, as is the shorter word.

clue.text: Epithet welcomed by US author this spoon-fed?

indicators.note: being welcomed by is being taken in, so the epithet goes inside

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a tag is a label or epithet

explanation.surface: An American writer receives a nickname and is spoon-fed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup is eaten with a spoon, so loosely it is food taken by spoon.

clue.text: Hairy biker's ultimate parting drink

indicators.note: parting means splitting the drink so the letter goes inside

parts.note: whiskey is the Irish or US spelling of whisky

indicators.note: ultimate means the last letter of the word biker

explanation.surface: A hairy biker takes a final drink on parting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hairy Bikers were a British TV cooking duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in whiskers, a bristly or hirsute face.
